failures.title: Subaru EZ36 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails
failures.goodYearsLine: The EZ36 improved over its production run. The post-2014 EZ36 (BS Outback, BN Legacy) received revised ECU calibration and improved cooling system components. Unlike the EJ25, the EZ36 does not have a reputation for head gasket failure - Subaru uses MLS gaskets and the failure rate is "significantly low". However, the engine is intolerant of overheating and cooling system neglect.

variants.title: EZ36 Variants - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: INTRO: The EZ36 (also known as EZ36D) is a single engine family with two primary variants distinguished by the transmission they were paired with and minor ECU revisions. The differences matter when buying a replacement. ### EZ36D - 2008-2014 (pre-facelift) - Fitted to: Subaru Tribeca WX (2008-2014), Subaru Legacy BM/BR (2009-2014), Subaru Outback BR (2009-2014) - Key technical difference: 3.6-litre petrol F6, DOHC, 24-valve. Dual AVCS (Active Valve Control System) on intake and exhaust camshafts. Compression ratio: 10.5:1. Power: 260 ps (191 kW) at 5,600 rpm. Torque: 350 Nm at 4,400 rpm. Paired with 5-speed automatic transmission. Die-cast aluminium block with 92.0 mm bores and 91.0 mm stroke. Features asymmetrical connecting rods for compact packaging. Timing chain (three chains) - no belt. Weight: 185 kg. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Cooling system failures are the primary concern on this variant. The 5-speed auto transmission can also contribute to higher engine load and heat. - Interchange note: Direct swap with post-2014 EZ36D requires ECU reflash and may need different transmission ancillaries. Ensure the replacement matches your model year and transmission type. ### EZ36D - 2014-2019 (post-facelift) - Fitted to: Subaru Legacy BN/BS (2014-2019), Subaru Outback BS (2014-2019) - Key technical difference: Same 3.6-litre petrol F6, DOHC, 24-valve. Power: 191 kW at 5,600 rpm. Torque: 350 Nm at 4,400 rpm. Paired with 6-speed CVT (Lineartronic) transmission. Revised ECU calibration and improved cooling system components. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Same cooling system and timing chain concerns as the earlier variant. The CVT transmission can place different load characteristics on the engine. Oil consumption can reach up to 1 litre per 2,000 km according to Subaru's official tolerance. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with the 2008-2014 variant - ECU, transmission, and wiring loom differ significantly. Only replace with another post-2014 EZ36D.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement EZ36 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used EZ36 makes sense only if it comes with documented evidence of cooling system maintenance (water pump, thermostat, radiator replaced within the last 50k miles) and regular oil changes using the correct 5W-30 synthetic oil. The EZ36 is intolerant of overheating - any used engine without cooling system history is a high-risk purchase. The recommended oil capacity is approximately 6.3-6.9 litres with filter. Used JDM EZ36 engines are available from £2,200-£3,200.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper EZ36 recon addresses the known weak points: new timing chain tensioner and guides, new water pump, new thermostat, new cam carrier seals, and a thorough cooling system flush. A 12-month warranty is standard. Reconditioned units are the sweet spot for most owners - you get the reliability upgrades without the cost of a full rebuild.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full EZ36 rebuild is justified when you own a high-value example (e.g., a well-specced Outback 3.6R or Tribeca) and want the engine to last another 150,000+ miles. An upgraded rebuild should include new piston rings (to address any oil consumption), new timing chain components, new cooling system components, and a thorough cylinder head inspection. For track use, consider an Accusump system or custom baffled oil pan to address oil starvation. Budget £4,500-£6,500 for a quality rebuild.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All of our vetted UK Subaru specialists offer supply-only or full supply-and-fit - nationwide delivery and recovery available, with warranties that cover both parts and labour.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The EZ36 sits in premium Subaru models - Outback 3.6R values range from £5,000-£18,000; Legacy 3.6R £4,000-£14,000; Tribeca £3,000-£8,000 depending on year and mileage. A reconditioned EZ36 at £3,200-£4,500 represents 20-50% of vehicle value - generally viable for most examples. However, for a high-mileage Tribeca (£3,000-£5,000), a full rebuild at £6,500 may exceed the vehicle's value. In those cases, evaluate the car's overall condition, rust, and transmission health before committing .

items.answer: A reconditioned EZ36 supply-only costs £3,200-£4,500, with fitted prices from £4,200-£5,700. Used units start from £2,200 supply-only. Rebuilt engines cost £4,500-£6,500 supply-only.

items.question: What are the most common EZ36 engine problems?
items.answer: The EZ36 suffers from overheating and cooling system failures (its most critical vulnerability), timing chain tensioner wear (100k+ miles), oil leaks from cam carriers and timing covers, and oil starvation under high-G cornering. Cooling system repairs cost £300-£800. Timing chain tensioner replacement costs £400-£800. Cam carrier resealing costs £800-£1,500. The EZ36 has a significantly low head gasket failure rate compared to the EJ25.

items.question: Which Subaru models use the EZ36 engine?
items.answer: The EZ36 was fitted to the Subaru Tribeca (2008-2014), Subaru Legacy 3.6R (2009-2019), and Subaru Outback 3.6R (2009-2019) in the UK. The pre-2014 EZ36 is paired with a 5-speed automatic. The post-2014 EZ36 is paired with a 6-speed CVT.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned EZ36?
items.answer: A reconditioned EZ36 is the safer choice - it includes a new timing chain tensioner, new cooling system components, new cam carrier seals, and a 12-month warranty. Used EZ36s are only recommended with documented cooling system service history. Any EZ36 without cooling system history is a high-risk purchase.

items.question: What's the difference between EZ36 and EZ30?
items.answer: The EZ36 is a 3.6-litre engine (vs EZ30's 3.0-litre) with larger bore (92.0mm vs 89.2mm) and longer stroke (91.0mm vs 80.0mm). The EZ36 produces more torque and power (260 hp vs 245 hp) but is more sensitive to cooling system neglect. They share the same basic architecture but are not directly interchangeable.
bullets: They share the same basic architecture but are not directly interchangeable.

items.question: How long does an EZ36 engine last?
items.answer: With regular maintenance (oil changes every 5k-6k miles using 5W-30, cooling system servicing every 50k miles), an EZ36 can exceed 150,000 miles. Cooling system neglect is the main limit on longevity. Timing chain tensioner may need replacement around 100k-150k miles. The EZ36 is generally robust when properly maintained.
